title: "Excel / ODS"
---

## Excel

Files ending in `.xlsx` or `.xls` are read with
[readxl](https://readxl.tidyverse.org/). Point `--output` (`-o`) at an `.xlsx`
file to write one with [writexl](https://docs.ropensci.org/writexl/). The older
`.xls` format can only be read.

### Reading and writing

```{term}
rush run -o sales.xlsx 'data.frame(
  product = c("Widget", "Gadget", "Doohickey"),
  q1 = c(100, 250, 75),
  q2 = c(120, 200, 90)
)'
rush run 'dplyr::mutate(df, total = q1 + q2)' sales.xlsx
```

Convert a CSV file to Excel:

```{term}
#| include: false
rush run -o mtcars.csv 'mtcars'
```

```{term}
rush convert -o mtcars.xlsx mtcars.csv
rush run 'nrow(df)' mtcars.xlsx
```

### `--input-sheet`

`rush` reads the first sheet of a workbook. To read another, pass its name or
its position to `--input-sheet`. readxl comes with an example workbook in the
`.xls` format that has several sheets:

```{term}
cp "$(rush run 'readxl::readxl_example("datasets.xls")')" datasets.xls
rush run 'readxl::excel_sheets("datasets.xls")'
rush run --input-sheet quakes 'head(df, 3)' datasets.xls
```

### `--output-sheet`

Name the sheet that is written (`Sheet1` by default):

```{term}
rush run --output-sheet cars -o cars.xlsx 'head(df, 3)' mtcars.csv
rush run 'readxl::excel_sheets("cars.xlsx")'
```

### Multiple sheets

A list of data frames is written as one sheet per element, named after the
list names. For example, split the cars by their number of cylinders:

```{term}
rush run -o split.xlsx 'split(df, ~ cyl)' mtcars.csv
rush run 'readxl::excel_sheets("split.xlsx")'
```

`--input-sheet` takes a number as the position of the sheet, so read the
sheet named `8` as the third sheet:

```{term}
rush run --input-sheet 3 'nrow(df)' split.xlsx
```

`rush convert` puts multiple files in one workbook, a sheet each. A database
becomes a sheet per table:

```{term}
rush run -o fast.csv 'dplyr::filter(df, hp > 200)' mtcars.csv
rush convert -o book.xlsx mtcars.csv fast.csv
rush run 'readxl::excel_sheets("book.xlsx")'
```

## ODS (OpenDocument Spreadsheet)

Files ending in `.ods`, as used by LibreOffice, are read and written with
[readODS](https://docs.ropensci.org/readODS/):

```{term}
rush convert -o sales.ods sales.xlsx
rush run 'df' sales.ods
```

`--input-sheet`, `--output-sheet`, and multiple sheets work for ODS files
too.

```{term}
#| include: false
rm -f mtcars.csv fast.csv sales.xlsx mtcars.xlsx datasets.xls cars.xlsx sales.ods
rm -f split.xlsx book.xlsx
```
